ap_calculus_ab-m01.stem: Let $f(x)=\ln\left(4x^{2}+1\right)e^{0.5x}$. What is the value of $f'(2)$?

options.why: Product rule with the chain rule on both the logarithm and the exponential, evaluated numerically.
Differentiates the logarithm without the inner derivative factor.
Product rule with the second term omitted.
Differentiates the exponential as e^{cx} without the factor c.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_ab
blueprint.concept: Derivative of a product of composite functions at a point, evaluated with a calculator
student_thinking: Recognize the function as a product of two composite functions
Apply the product and chain rules to get f' symbolically
Evaluate f' at the given point with a graphing calculator

key_conditions.condition: f is differentiable at the point (logarithm argument positive)
key_conditions.evidence: 4x^2+1 > 0 for all x, exponential defined everywhere

misconceptions.description: drops the inner derivative of the logarithm argument
uses only one term of the product rule
forgets the factor c from differentiating the exponent

verification.independent_path: symbolic derivative (sympy) cross-checked by a central finite difference with step 1e-6 on the original function

ap_calculus_ab-m02.stem: The function $f(x)=xe^{x/2}+2x$ is continuous on $[0,2]$. By the Intermediate Value Theorem there is a number $c$ in $(0,2)$ with $f(c)=4.7$. What is the value of $c$?

options.why: Takes the midpoint of the interval as the solution.
Solves f(x)=k/2 instead of f(x)=k.
Solve f(x)=k on the interval with a graphing calculator (f is increasing, so the solution is unique).
Interpolates linearly between f(0) and the right-endpoint value.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_ab
blueprint.concept: Use the Intermediate Value Theorem guarantee and solve f(c)=k numerically
student_thinking: Check the function is continuous and k lies between f(0) and f(b)
Set up f(x)=k on the interval
Solve the equation numerically with a graphing calculator

key_conditions.condition: f is continuous on the closed interval and strictly increasing so the solution is unique

misconceptions.description: assumes the solution is the midpoint of the interval
assumes f is linear between endpoints
solves for the wrong target value

verification.independent_path: brentq root (generation) cross-checked by a hand-written bisection with 80 halvings on the same function

ap_calculus_ab-m03.stem: The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0.5xy$ with $f(0)=2$. What is the value of $f(3)$?

options.why: Integrates kx dx as kx^2 and forgets the factor 1/2.
Adds the integral of the right side instead of exponentiating.
Separate variables, integrate to get ln|y| = kx^2/2 + C, apply the initial condition, and evaluate with a calculator.
Treats x as a constant when integrating, giving an exponent kx.

blueprint.subject: ap_calculus_ab
blueprint.concept: Particular solution of a separable differential equation evaluated at a point
student_thinking: Separate the variables dy/y = kx dx
Integrate both sides and apply the initial condition
Evaluate the particular solution at the requested value with a calculator

key_conditions.condition: y stays positive on the interval so ln|y| = ln y
key_conditions.evidence: y(0)=2>0 and the solution A*exp(k x^2/2) is positive

misconceptions.description: forgets the 1/2 when integrating x
treats x as constant during integration
adds instead of exponentiating

verification.independent_path: closed form from separation cross-checked by adaptive Runge-Kutta numerical integration (rtol 1e-11)
